title: Reduction preserves a regular single module in degree zero
statement: For an adic principal datum d on a domain A with nonzero generator π, let H be a completed-coefficient module sheaf with injective π action on sections. Every completed finite reduction of H[0] has zero cohomology in every degree other than zero.

source.place: Order 1429, sufficient uniformizer-injectivity criterion; normalized principal quotient triangle (Stacks Tag 06YU).

proof.text: The single-object homology comparison identifies degree-zero cohomology with H, carrying the injective scalar action across a linear isomorphism. All other cohomology objects are zero and have subsingleton sections, so their scalar action is injective as well. Apply the canonical cohomology comparison for principal reduction in every degree. Outside degree zero its source is extension of a zero object and is therefore zero. No finiteness or flatness assumption on H is used.

lean.statement:
theorem principalReduction_single_isConcentrated
    (T : Scheme.{u}) {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) (π : A) (hI : d.ideal = Ideal.span {π})
    (hπ : π ≠ 0) (H : pbcModules T (pbcAdicCompletion T d))
    (hinj : ∀ U : T.ProEtᵒᵖ, Function.Injective (fun x : H.val.obj U ↦
      (CompletedConstantReduction.base T d.ideal ≫
        CompletedConstantReduction.completedComparison T d.ideal d.quotientFinite).hom.app U
          ((adicLisseConstantUnit T A).app U π) • x)) (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ q : ℤ, q ≠ 0 → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj
      ((pbcDerivedExtend (pbcAdicProjection T d n)).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj H)))
